title: Executive decision and boundaries
specification_text:
1. Executive decision and boundaries
Objective: demonstrate that application-log suppression during simulated OAuth token replay does not necessarily eliminate independently observed evidence, and test whether invocation-bound, completeness-aware reconciliation improves detection compared with simpler log-based baselines.
Do not claim that an AWS Lambda extension is independent of a compromised Lambda process, that CloudTrail records arbitrary outbound SaaS requests, that a hash proves event truth, or that OAuth token revocation always takes effect immediately.
Definition of success
Review 2: deployed AWS Lambda application, controlled OAuth test API, legitimate request, disposable-token replay, suppressed application log, independent API-side audit event, correlation finding, timestamped demonstration and evidence.
Final capstone: IBER state machine, completeness windows, immutable evidence archive, safe response workflow, repeatable attack/fault scenarios, quantitative baselines, ablation study, cost/latency measurements, and documented limitations.
Non-goals: scraping live third-party credentials, production SaaS exploitation, universal attribution of all outbound traffic, guarantee of instantaneous detection, or perfect reconstruction from nonexistent evidence.
blocker: Live Review-2 and final acceptance require approved AWS account

Boundary
Attacker capability
Defensive assumption

title: Logical architecture and data flows
specification_text:
3. Logical architecture and data flows
Ingress: client -> API Gateway -> Lambda integration -> mock SaaS resource API. OAuth: mock authorization server issues short-lived scoped test token, stored in Secrets Manager for lab integration. Evidence: Lambda intent emitter, API Gateway access logs, supported CloudTrail events, Lambda platform telemetry, mock SaaS audit emitter. Collector: independently permissioned API Gateway/Lambda -> SQS -> normalizer -> DynamoDB correlation state and S3 Object Lock archive. Detection: EventBridge or SQS-triggered reconciler -> findings -> Step Functions response -> responder Lambda -> mock provider revoke/disable integration. Investigation: archive reader -> ordered timeline with confidence and gaps -> report.
Trust-sensitive architecture decisions
External SaaS audit record must originate at the test API service, not be copied from the compromised Lambda log.
For the first milestone, use a mock provider and mock SaaS API on separately permissioned infrastructure; real sandbox provider is optional later.
If intent is emitted solely by compromised application, it may be missing or fabricated. Detect against independently issued authorizations and external actions; label unverifiable cases inconclusive.
No guarantee of exact cross-provider request matching: use provider request ID where supported, else bounded identity/operation/resource/time matching with lower confidence.
Hash-chain ordering must be defined per collector partition or single writer; global ordering across parallel writers is not assumed.
blocker: Confirm deployed resource flows

title: Canonical event contracts
specification_text:
6. Canonical event contracts
Evidence event v1 fields
event_id (UUID), schema_version, run_id, scenario_id, invocation_id (nullable), action_id (nullable), source_type, source_trust_tier, event_type, operation, resource_pseudonym, credential_fingerprint (HMAC), event_time_utc, collector_received_at_utc, provider_request_id (nullable), correlation_key (nullable), event_payload_hash, collector_receipt_id, source_health, integrity_version, trace_context (nullable).
Use UTC ISO-8601 timestamps. Keep event_time and received_at separate. Define source-specific required fields, schema validation, dead-letter handling, and duplicate behavior. Store raw original event and canonicalized normalized event separately; version normalization rules.
Detection finding v1
finding_id, run_id, affected_identity, evidence_event_ids[], classification (CONSISTENT, PENDING, SUSPICIOUS, CORROBORATED_SUSPECTED_ABUSE, INCONCLUSIVE), severity, rationale_codes[], missing_sources[], confidence_basis, decision_at, attack_ground_truth_reference (evaluation only), response_requested, response_verified_at, residual_uncertainty.
State transitions
PENDING -> CONSISTENT when required corroboration arrives; PENDING -> SUSPICIOUS when evidence contradicts authorization; PENDING -> INCONCLUSIVE if source unhealthy or coverage inadequate; SUSPICIOUS -> CORROBORATED_SUSPECTED_ABUSE when independently corroborated; late arrivals cause an auditable re-evaluation, not silent overwrite.

title: Algorithm specification and test cases
specification_text:
9. Algorithm specification and test cases
Matching precedence: (1) explicit provider_request_id and issued authorization ID, (2) invocation_id/action_id propagated through a trusted gateway where available, (3) bounded identity + operation + resource + time candidate set. Ambiguous matches remain ambiguous. Avoid treating correlation based only on time as definitive proof.
Deadline selection: estimate per-source arrival distributions on benign calibration runs; define D_source = chosen percentile + safety margin; record exact parameters and calibration data. Late events trigger revision and are measured as such. Do not hardcode a 5-second guarantee.
Test ID
Stimulus
Expected behavior
T01
Normal authorized API read
CONSISTENT
T02
Replay from independent test client with suppressed app log
SUSPICIOUS then corroborated when evidence supports
T03
Benign app logger disabled, no replay
INCONCLUSIVE or benign fault, not confirmed abuse
T04
Provider audit delayed
PENDING then correct late revision
T05
Duplicate SQS event
One logical evidence record
T06
Out-of-order audit records
Stable result after window closes
T07
Collector down
Health alert; no false certainty
T08
Expired/invalid token replay
Record denied action, do not call successful exfiltration
T09

Access denied; preserve evidence

Response status failed/unverified
T11

No automatic malicious verdict solely for volume
T12

No cross-invocation false association

title: Research evaluation protocol
specification_text:
10. Research evaluation protocol
Research questions: RQ1 attack detection under suppressed logs; RQ2 false-positive robustness to benign telemetry faults; RQ3 latency/overhead/cost; RQ4 integrity and reconstruction accuracy. Ground truth must be generated by an isolated scenario runner, never inferred from detector output.
Baselines: B0 application logs only; B1 independent external audit only; B2 simple fixed-time missing-event rule; B3 full IBER. Ablations: remove completeness windows, invocation-bound matching, provider audit, integrity verification separately. Use separate calibration and held-out test runs; randomize execution order and document AWS region/time-of-day.
Metrics: precision, recall, F1, false-positive rate, inconclusive rate, detection p50/p95, evidence delivery p50/p95, containment verification time, reconstruction precision/order accuracy, modified-evidence detection rate, billed Lambda duration, cost per 1000 invocations. Report confidence intervals and denominators.
Initial engineering targets (not claims): >=90% recall on controlled replay scenarios, <=5% false-positive rate on held-out benign/fault runs, p95 <=10 seconds only where independent evidence arrives promptly; otherwise report observed bound and why.
blocker: Independent scenario holdout and cloud cost/overhead

title: Deployment, operations and handover runbook
specification_text:
13. Deployment, operations and handover runbook
Prerequisites
AWS account with appropriate permissions; select and document one region; AWS CLI configured using temporary/SSO credentials.
AWS SAM CLI, Python supported runtime, Git, pytest, and a clean test account.
Budget alerts, resource tags Project=SealedTelemetry and Environment=Lab.
Synthetic records, test-only OAuth issuer, and no production external SaaS credentials.
Standard operator sequence
1. git clone <team-repo>; git checkout <review2-tag>; verify README and prerequisites.
2. cp .env.example .env; populate only non-secret configuration; use Secrets Manager for token material.
3. sam build; sam deploy --guided using documented stack name and region.
4. python scripts/seed_lab.py to provision synthetic identities/records; record run_id.
5. pytest tests/unit; pytest tests/integration; run the normal scenario and check API response.
6. python scripts/run_demo.py --scenario normal; capture evidence IDs and timing.
7. python scripts/run_demo.py --scenario replay-suppression; inspect finding and provider-side audit.
8. python scripts/run_demo.py --scenario benign-log-failure; confirm uncertainty classification.
9. Export sanitized results and evidence manifest; tag Git commit and save environment details.
10. Run cleanup script and sam delete; verify retained evidence policy and residual charges before deleting any protected resources.
Commands above are planned interface contracts: scripts do not exist until implemented. Update this runbook with tested, exact command syntax, stack outputs and expected results. Object Lock retention can prevent deletion; use a separate ephemeral development archive with appropriate lifecycle and compliance review.
Handover checkpoint template

• Implemented features with passing test IDs and evidence links
• Open blockers, assumptions and known security limitations

title: Review-2 oral defense: anticipated questions
specification_text:
14. Review-2 oral defense: anticipated questions
Is detection real time?
Near-real-time only when independent evidence arrives quickly; report measured end-to-end latency and distinguish detection after invocation.
Does everything finish before Lambda terminates?
No. The original invocation can finish while asynchronous ingestion, reconciliation, containment and forensics continue outside Lambda.
Why not CloudWatch alone?
Application logs may be suppressed; platform logs are incomplete for outbound SaaS operations; independent API-side evidence adds a different trust boundary.
What is novel?
A testable invocation-bound, completeness-aware reconciliation mechanism with explicit uncertainty and cross-source evidence, subject to prior-work comparison and ablations.
Can you prove the token was stolen?
The controlled scenario ground truth proves simulated exposure and replay; independent audit may corroborate unauthorized use but not always the theft mechanism.
Can you revoke immediately?
Only where the provider supports it; request and verify revocation separately. Do not equate API acknowledgment with immediate rejection.
What if both logs disappear?
Report inconclusive if no trustworthy witness exists; do not invent missing events.
What is the actual serverless benefit?
Event-driven processing and pay-per-use orchestration, while acknowledging cold starts, asynchronous delay and service cost.
blocker: Human defense rehearsal

title: Architecture deployment profiles
specification_text:
17. Architecture deployment profiles
Profile A (Review 2): one isolated AWS sandbox account, separate workload and security IAM roles, API Gateway + workload Lambda, mock OAuth/SaaS service with separate audit writer, collector Lambda, SQS, DynamoDB, S3 and a detector Lambda. Profile B (final): preferably separate workload and security AWS accounts, cross-account event delivery, S3 Object Lock with protected retention, Step Functions responder, CloudTrail and provider audit integration.
Critical limitation: the workload cannot reliably attest to its own intent after full compromise. An intent record is a claim, not proof. Corroboration must come from a source the compromised workload cannot edit. A mock provider can provide ground truth for the prototype; real providers differ in audit coverage and revocation semantics.

title: Review-2 failure contingencies
specification_text:
20. Review-2 failure contingencies
If the AWS deployment fails: use pre-recorded traces from the same versioned build and show the failed deployment logs; do not represent a recording as live.
If CloudTrail is delayed: show platform/ingress/provider evidence and explicitly identify CloudTrail as asynchronous supplementary evidence.
If the detector has no finding: inspect correlation IDs, time-window configuration, SQS DLQ, and collector health before changing thresholds.
If mock provider audit is unavailable: stop the claim of independent corroboration; demo only ingestion health and mark the security result incomplete.
If the simulated replay is rejected: verify test token scope, expiry and intended mock resource; never bypass controls on a real provider.

specification_text:
22. End-to-end event and decision contract
EvidenceEvent v1 mandatory fields: schema_version, event_id, run_id, source_id, trust_tier, event_type, event_time_utc, collector_received_at_utc, invocation_id (nullable), action_id (nullable), provider_request_id (nullable), actor_pseudonym, credential_fingerprint (nullable), operation, resource_pseudonym, outcome, collector_receipt_id, canonical_hash. Never persist bearer tokens or refresh tokens.
Finding v1 mandatory fields: finding_id, run_id, first_observed_at, decided_at, state, rule_version, correlated_event_ids, missing_expected_sources, source_health_snapshot, reason_codes, confidence_category, response_policy, response_status, reconstruction_status.
State invariants: PENDING is not an attack; INCONCLUSIVE is not benign; CORROBORATED requires independent supporting observations; receipt time never replaces source time; a detector decision must retain evidence IDs and rule version; later evidence may supersede but must not erase prior decisions.
blocker: Live versioned evidence export

title: Correlation algorithm: implementable pseudocode
specification_text:
23. Correlation algorithm: implementable pseudocode
on_evidence(event):    validate_schema_and_source(event)    persist_idempotently(event.event_id)    update_source_health(event.source_id, event.collector_received_at)    keys = candidate_keys(event.invocation_id, event.action_id,                          event.provider_request_id, event.actor_pseudonym)    for case in find_candidate_cases(keys, bounded_time_window):        reconcile(case)reconcile(case):    observed = independently_observed_provider_actions(case)    authorized = match_to_expected_actions(case, strict_ids_first=True)    if observed and not authorized:        if corroboration_sufficient(case):            decide(case, "CORROBORATED", reason="UNMATCHED_EXTERNAL_ACTION")        elif deadlines_open(case):            decide(case, "PENDING", reason="WAITING_FOR_EVIDENCE")        else:            decide(case, "SUSPICIOUS", reason="UNMATCHED_LOW_CONFIDENCE")    elif missing_required_evidence(case):        if deadlines_open(case):            decide(case, "PENDING", reason="LATE_SOURCE")        elif source_unhealthy(case):            decide(case, "INCONCLUSIVE", reason="COLLECTOR_FAILURE")        else:            decide(case, "SUSPICIOUS", reason="EVIDENCE_GAP")    else:        decide(case, "CONSISTENT", reason="MATCHED_ACTION")    append_decision_history(case)

25. Experiment design, reproducibility and reporting

title: Architecture principles and hard security boundaries
specification_text:
32. Architecture principles and hard security boundaries
Workload account is assumed compromisable; security-owned collector and storage are not writable by the workload except through a narrow append-only authenticated ingestion API.
Application-intent events are untrusted claims; mock provider audit is the authoritative source for successful mock SaaS actions, not for attacker identity or motivation.
Token replay from outside the instrumented application may have no invocation ID. Detect as unmatched provider activity; do not manufacture invocation correlation.
CloudTrail captures supported AWS API actions, not arbitrary outbound HTTPS requests. Telemetry API extension runs in the Lambda environment and is not independently tamperproof.
Raw bearer/refresh tokens must never enter audit records. A security-side keyed pseudonym is preferred; log only token ID/jti if the mock issuer defines it.
All evidence transport is at-least-once with possible delay. No guaranteed real-time detection; report observed distribution and evidence source coverage.
No service should assume that missing logs prove theft. Treat collector failure, retention gaps, and clock skew explicitly.
blocker: Live boundaries; no extension attestation or SaaS egress CloudTrail claim

title: Concrete request and event sequence
specification_text:
36. Concrete request and event sequence
1. Scenario runner creates run_id and ground-truth record in a separate restricted dataset.
2. Legitimate client invokes API Gateway, which assigns request ID and invokes workload Lambda.
3. Workload Lambda obtains disposable scoped credential and sends INTENT_CREATED to collector; failure is recorded locally but must not be trusted as sole evidence.
4. Workload calls mock SaaS endpoint with token. Mock SaaS validates signature or opaque registry, audience, scope, expiry and revoked state.
5. Mock SaaS commits the synthetic operation and independently appends PROVIDER_ACTION, ideally with a provider request ID and token ID.
6. Collector authenticates event source, validates schema, stamps receipt time and event ID, enqueues SQS; invalid events go to quarantine without sensitive payload exposure.
7. Normalizer conditionally writes DynamoDB index and canonical raw record to S3; retries are idempotent.
8. Detector opens/updates case, joins source evidence, waits until per-source deadline and records a versioned decision.
9. For suspicious/corroborated case, EventBridge triggers Step Functions; policy gate chooses alert only or controlled containment.
10. Responder requests mock revocation and disables integration if required; verifies subsequent synthetic calls fail.
11. Report generator emits evidence timeline, checksums, gaps, source health, response and recovery outcomes.
12. Evaluation harness joins ground truth with findings after test completion and calculates latency, error rates and cost.
blocker: Cloud end-to-end causal observations

title: Infrastructure-as-code deployment ordering
specification_text:
38. Infrastructure-as-code deployment ordering
Bootstrap AWS sandbox: account/region selection, AWS CLI profile, billing budget, MFA, resource tags and KMS access strategy.
Deploy security data layer first: KMS key, S3 evidence bucket, DynamoDB tables, SQS and DLQ, alarms.
Deploy security ingress API and collector with authenticated source identity; test unauthorized calls and oversized payload rejection.
Deploy mock OAuth issuer, token registry, mock SaaS API and provider audit writer with independent permissions.
Deploy workload API Gateway, Lambda, secret, tracing and minimal runtime IAM role.
Deploy normalizer, detector, scheduled pending-case sweeper and versioned rules.
Deploy EventBridge response routing, Step Functions, responder and sanitized report generation.
Run automated smoke tests, access-denial tests, scenario suite and teardown rehearsal.
blocker: Account/region/artifact bucket/service role and change-set approval

title: Resource configuration checklist
specification_text:
39. Resource configuration checklist
Lambda: memory/timeout/concurrency chosen by measured load; structured JSON logging; safe environment variables; no raw token output; X-Ray sampling if enabled.
API Gateway: route authorization, access logs without Authorization headers, request size limits, throttling and CORS only where necessary.
SQS: visibility timeout exceeds consumer runtime with margin; DLQ redrive policy; retention aligned with incident-response needs; age and DLQ alarms.
DynamoDB: PAY_PER_REQUEST for low-volume prototype, point-in-time recovery if budget allows, conditional writes for event_id, GSIs for run_id and provider_request_id.
S3: block public access, versioning, encryption, bucket policy denying workload principals, lifecycle/retention review, Object Lock on dedicated evidence bucket if enabled.
KMS: separate key policies and audit of use; no workload permission to change key policy; account for recovery from key loss.
CloudTrail: configure only relevant AWS management/data events and document coverage and cost; do not mistake it for SaaS HTTP egress visibility.
EventBridge/Step Functions: retry and idempotency for response, approval path for uncertain findings, record every transition.
CloudWatch: alarms on collector error rate, queue age, DLQ depth, detector failures, responder failures and budget.
blocker: Real service propagation, throttling, retention and cost

title: Deadline-aware decision specification
specification_text:
40. Deadline-aware decision specification
Maintain source-specific lateness estimates from benign calibration runs. For each expected evidence source, configure a maximum wait based on measured delivery percentiles plus a documented margin. At deadline, record missing source and health state. Re-evaluate if late evidence arrives; append a new decision version instead of rewriting history.
Condition
Decision
Automated response
Authorized provider action matched to intent; healthy sources
CONSISTENT
None
Provider action unmatched; matching still possible before deadline
PENDING
None
Unmatched provider action plus corroborating evidence of misuse
CORROBORATED_SUSPECTED_ABUSE
Only if tested policy threshold met
Missing app log but provider action authorized or absent
SUSPICIOUS_TELEMETRY_GAP or INCONCLUSIVE
Alert, no automatic revocation
Collector unhealthy or audit coverage unknown
INCONCLUSIVE
Repair evidence path and investigate
Late event contradicts previous decision
REVISED decision with provenance
Reassess response; preserve original decision
blocker: Benign AWS percentile calibration; bounds remain explicit

title: Security tests beyond the happy path
specification_text:
41. Security tests beyond the happy path
Token replay from a separate test client with no invocation ID must be detected through provider-side observation, not fabricated correlation.
Attack harness must not hold permissions to edit security account archive or the mock provider audit writer.
Clock skew ±30 seconds, out-of-order arrival, duplicated event IDs, missing provider request IDs and dropped queue messages must be tested.
Verify that the application can suppress its own logs without deleting provider audit; explicitly test the converse (provider audit unavailable).
Ensure an untrusted client cannot forge provider audit via the same ingress path used by the application.
Verify token expiry, wrong audience, wrong scope, revoked token and failed revocation API paths.
Demonstrate false-positive handling for benign application logging failure and collector outage.
Run tamper tests against copied test evidence; record that cryptographic integrity does not establish completeness or truth.
Run clean-room redeployment from source and verify rollback and cleanup scripts.
blocker: Real cloud fault/security/clean-deploy checks
